title: Sodium arsenite induces a p21-dependent G2/M cell cycle arrest via ROS-mediated DNA damage in HEK-293 cells
content:
Abstract
Arsenic is a ubiquitous environmental toxicant closely linked to multiple adverse biological effects and health impairments. In this study, we investigated the effect of exposure to sodium arsenite on reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, DNA damage response, and G2/M arrest in HEK-293 cells. The results showed that exposure to sodium arsenite induced a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS levels. Assessment of DNA damage via γ-H2AX detection and comet assay revealed that arsenite treatment also enhanced γ-H2AX expression and tailed DNA content markedly in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, flow cytometric analysis confirmed that arsenite concurrently triggered pronounced G2/M arrest in HEK-293 cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that exposure to sodium arsenite led to ROS-induced DNA damage in HEK-293 cells, which further led to G2/M arrest via activating the ATM-p53-p21 pathway. Notably, arsenite-induced G2/M arrest in HEK-293 cells was predominantly mediated by p21 upregulation, independent of Cdc25C-CDK1 pathway. This work deepens our comprehensive insight into the regulation of G2/M arrest upon arsenite exposure and lays a mechanistic basis for subsequent studies in more physiologically pertinent and tissue-specific models.
